name: Observable Universe
tagline: The causal horizon — everything light has had time to reach us from in 13.8 billion years.
history: The observable universe is the spherical volume of space from which light has had time to reach us since the Big Bang — not the universe's edge, but the horizon of our information about it. Its 46.5-billion-light-year radius reflects the expansion of space itself while the light was travelling: objects now there emitted their photons when they were much closer. Everything inside this shell — every supercluster, every galaxy, every star — is all we can ever causally know.
